newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe experts seek ban of Boeing merger, source says.
newsitem.headline: Europe experts seek ban of Boeing merger, source says.

text.p: Antitrust experts from European Union member nations unanimously recommended Wednesday banning the planned $14 billion merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., an industry source said.

The source was reading from an official opinion agreed on by the experts from the 15 EU countries. The European Commission is widely expected to follow the advice at its regular meeting next week after Boeing, the world's largest aircraft maker, failed to adequately address concerns in Europe that the deal would harm fair competition in the EU.
"The advisory committee again unanimously supported the commission view that the remedies offered were unsufficient," the source said, speaking on the condition of anonymity.
Commission officials were not immediately available to comment. The EU executive body was widely expected to block the merger at its regular meeting next Wednesday.

A majority of committee members said Boeing's proposals to try to resolve European objections to the merger "showed progress," the source said. European officials have said the merged company would dominate the market for aircraft, hurting Airbus Industrie, the European aircraft maker.

German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said Wednesday that Boeing's offer to report regularly to the EU about cross-subsidies from the military business to the civilian aircraft operations, along with other commitments, were not enough to win EU approval.
